title: Job 30
paragraphs: ¹ "But now men younger than I mock me — men whose fathers I would not have trusted to guard my dogs. ² What good was the strength of their hands to me? They were men in whom all vigor had wasted away. ³ Gaunt with want and hunger, they gnawed the dry ground in the dark wastelands. ⁴ They picked saltwort from the bushes and dined on the roots of broom trees. ⁵ They were outcasts from the community — people shouted after them as after a thief.

⁶ They were driven to live in the gullies and ravines, in holes in the earth and among the rocks. ⁷ They brayed among the bushes and huddled together under the nettles. ⁸ They were senseless, nameless men, driven out of the land. ⁹ And now I have become their taunt, their byword. ¹⁰ They detest me and keep their distance, yet they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

¹¹ Now that God has unstrung me and brought me low, they have thrown off all restraint. ¹² On my right the mob rises up; they set traps for my feet and build their siege ramps against me. ¹³ They tear up my path; they advance to finish me off without anyone to stop them. ¹⁴ They rush in through a wide breach; they roll in amid the ruins. ¹⁵ Terrors crash over me; my dignity is swept away like the wind and my safety vanishes like a cloud.

¹⁶ And now my life drains away; days of suffering grip me. ¹⁷ At night my bones ache with pain that never sleeps; ¹⁸ in the grip of my sickness my garment is disfigured; it binds around me like the collar of my robe. ¹⁹ He has cast me into the mud; I have become like dust and ashes. ²⁰ I cry out to you, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you only stare at me.

²¹ You have turned on me without mercy; with the strength of your hand you attack me. ²² You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm. ²³ I know you will bring me to my death — to the place appointed for everyone who lives. ²⁴ Yet surely no one raises a hand against the broken when they cry out for help in their ruin. ²⁵ Have I not wept for those in trouble? Was my heart not grieved for the poor?

²⁶ Yet when I looked for good, evil came; when I hoped for light, darkness fell. ²⁷ My heart churns without rest; days of suffering rise up to meet me. ²⁸ I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help. ²⁹ I am a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches. ³⁰ My skin has turned black and peeling; my bones burn with fever.
³¹ My harp is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.
